html:
SMTO-SKL-0027 — SMTO couldn't confirm whether your calendar change happened

GUID: 13e116f2-5d0f-5889-b34d-0575fdcad155
Slug: google-calendar-mutation-outcome-unknown
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • SMTO sent the change to Google but couldn't confirm the result, so it may or may not have happened. Guests may also have been emailed. SMTO did not send it again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether the earlier action already happened: open Google Calendar and look at the event or calendar. Was it created, changed, moved, deleted or answered as you asked? Google may have made the change even though SMTO didn't get confirmation.
  2. You can also ask SMTO to read that event again; the error details name the calendar and event it was working on. A fresh read shows the event's real current state.
  3. If you asked for a new event and don't see it, wait a minute and check again before asking SMTO to create it. A new event can take a moment to appear, and asking too soon could create a duplicate.
  4. Only if the change is clearly missing, ask SMTO to make it again. Repeating a change that already happened can create duplicates or send guests extra emails.

What success looks like

  • Google Calendar shows the event exactly once, in the state you wanted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to repeat the change until you've confirmed it isn't already in your calendar.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Google Calendar write got a server error, lost its response, or returned an event ID or ETag that could not confirm the change, and the follow-up read could not prove the outcome; Google may already have applied it.

What this means

  • A write receives a server failure or loses a reliable response, or its returned event identity/ETag cannot confirm the mutation. The provider may already have applied the mutation. Inspect the exact retained resource/correlation and reconcile its state before issuing another write; the diagnostic never retries it.

Why this can happen

  • A write receives a server failure or loses a reliable response, or its returned event identity/ETag cannot confirm the mutation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact event and any destination calendar using the recorded operation identity.

How to fix it

  • Do not repeat the mutation. Using the calendar_id and event_id (and destination_calendar_id for a move) in the error details, read the event and compare its status, ETag and fields, or the self attendee's response, with the intended change. A create used a runtime-derived event ID tagged in extendedProperties.private.smtoRequest; wait and read that ID before considering a new create. For calendar or calendar-list writes (no event IDs), list google_calendar.calendars or read calendar_get/calendar_list_get to check the result.
  • Do not repeat the mutation. Read the returned exact calendar_id and event_id (and destination_calendar_id for move), then reconcile the event, ETag or self response. A create uses a runtime-generated event ID; wait and inspect that ID before considering a new create.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not repeat the mutation. Read the returned exact calendar_id and event_id (and destination_calendar_id for move), then reconcile the event, ETag or self response. A create uses a runtime-generated event ID; wait and inspect that ID before considering a new create.

How to verify the fix

  • The event's actual state is reconciled before any new mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • The provider may already have applied the mutation. Inspect the exact retained resource/correlation and reconcile its state before issuing another write; the diagnostic never retries it.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
